The game is complete and verified. All requirements are implemented in the single file **`snake_ollama-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-a6b-q4_01.html`** (750 lines, JS syntax validated with Node):

**What's in the file:**

- **Classic Snake on a 30×30 grid** — rendered on a 600×600 HTML canvas with a dark theme, subtle grid lines, rounded snake segments, and glowing food.
- **Continuous movement** — both snakes move every tick (~110ms) via a `requestAnimationFrame` accumulator; direction queue prevents 180° reversals from fast key presses.
- **Growth & death** — eating food adds a segment; hitting a wall, any snake body (own or opponent's), or a head-to-head collision ends the game for the affected snake(s).
- **Keyboard controls** — Player 1: WASD, Player 2: Arrow keys (only bound for snakes not CPU-controlled).
- **CPU AI** — BFS pathfinding to the food (walls + snake bodies as obstacles, moving tail treated as free); if no path exists, it picks the safe direction that maximizes reachable free space via flood-fill.
- **Three game modes** (menu buttons at lines 167–169):
  - `pvp` — Human vs Human
  - `cpu-p` — CPU vs Human (snake 1 is CPU, you control the magenta snake with arrows)
  - `cpu-cpu` — CPU vs CPU (spectate)
- **Live score HUD** — color-coded scores and lengths for both snakes shown during play.
- **Start menu & game over screens** — overlays with mode selection; the game-over screen shows the winner (or draw) and final scores.
- **Restart with keypress** — Space/Enter restarts the current mode; Esc returns to the menu.

Open the file in any modern browser to play — no server or dependencies needed.

conversation.contentPreview: Write a snake game in javascript, css, html in one file. Build a classic Snake game on a 30x30 grid. The snake moves continuously in one of four directions and grows when eating food. If it hits a wall or itself, the game ends. Implement keyboard controls for player movement. Add a CPU-controlled snake mode that automatically searches for food. Add the three game modes: human vs human, cpu vs human, cpu vs cpu. Display the score during gameplay. Include a start menu and game over screen. Allow restarting the game with a keypress. Use file name "snake_ollama-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-a6b-q4_01.html"
I'll create the snake game as a single self-contained HTML file.

{"path":"snake_ollama-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-a6b-q4_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete single-file Snake game (HTML + CSS + JavaScript all in one file). Requirements:

1. Classic Snake on a 30x30 grid rendered on an HTML5 canvas (cell size ~20px, so 600x600 canvas). Dark theme, modern look with subtle grid lines, rounded snake segments, glowing food.

2. Two snakes play simultaneously on the same board (competitive):
   - Snake 1 (green) starts on the left side, facing right.
   - Snake 2 (magenta/orange) starts on the right side, facing left.
   - Snakes move continuously at a fixed tick interval (e.g. 110ms via setInterval or requestAnimationFrame accumulator).
   - Each snake grows by 1 segment when it eats food.
   - A snake dies if its head hits a wall OR hits any body segment (its own or the other snake's). Head-to-head collision kills both.
   - Food: one food item at a time; when eaten, a new one spawns in a random empty cell.

3. Three game modes selectable in the start menu:
   - "Human vs Human": Player 1 uses WASD, Player 2 uses Arrow keys.
   - "CPU vs Human": Snake 1 is CPU-controlled, Player 2 uses Arrow keys.
   - "CPU vs CPU": Both snakes CPU-controlled (spectate mode).

4. CPU AI: automatically searches for food using BFS pathfinding on the grid avoiding walls and snake bodies (treat the tail cell that will move away as safe). If no path to food exists, pick any safe adjacent cell that maximizes free space (flood-fill count). Never reverse into itself.

5. Score display during gameplay: HUD at top showing each snake's score (score = food eaten) and length, with color-coded labels.

6. Start menu overlay: title "SNAKE", three mode buttons (Human vs Human, CPU vs Human, CPU vs CPU), and control instructions (WASD for P1, Arrows for P2).

7. Game over screen overlay: shows winner (or draw), both scores, "Press SPACE or ENTER to restart" and "Press ESC for menu". Restart with keypress restarts the same mode; ESC returns to menu.

8. Clean, well-structured vanilla JS (no frameworks). Use a game state machine: 'menu', 'playing', 'gameover'. Prevent default scrolling on arrow/space keys. Handle direction queue so quick key presses within one tick don't allow 180-degree reversal.

Make the code complete, polished and working — no placeholders or TODOs."}
